Introduction

Although humanity has set foot on the moon and launched spaceships to planets thousands of miles away from earth, how many people have been to the wild valleys, full of strange flowers and plants in the Snow Mountains, or contacted and learned from the saints and sages in retreat there?

For Europeans and Americans, Tuyet Son is just a mountain range similar to hundreds of thousands of other mountain ranges on the earth's surface, but Asians view Tuyet Son as a sacred place, with a great influence on the fate of humanity. While Asians revere the sages who hermit here and often go to great lengths to climb passes and wade streams to find teachers, Europeans and Americans only consider the monks living in the snowy mountains as uneducated people, full of superstition.

In the early twentieth century, an English bishop, Mr. C.W. Leadbeater went to Tuyet Son to study the spiritual tradition here. For Asians, searching for a monk to study religion is not a strange thing, but it is an extremely rare event for a Westerner to venture to Tuyet Son to learn from the hermits here. More specifically, this person is a prestigious bishop, governing a large parish in England. He put aside narrow prejudices and short-sighted opinions about Eastern traditions at that time to learn about ancient truths that have been carefully preserved for thousands of years.

After many years of research, he returned to England and shared his experiences through many lectures and books about the sages of Snow Mountain. He wrote: "I don't ask people to believe much of what I present, I just want you to calmly meditate and if you cannot accept it at this time, I hope it will cause some spiritual inspiration so that in the future, you can understand it more clearly." According to him, studying with the sages on Tuyet Son strengthened his religious beliefs more firmly about things that before, although he learned through the Western tradition, he could not really experience.

He concluded that in the universe there are still laws that never change or truths that have been proven and taught to students by ancient teachers. These teachings are summarized and taught through major religions, but over time, some things have been misunderstood or taught incorrectly, losing their true value, causing religion instead of being alive to become dry and degenerate into a rigid form of dogma. Therefore, not only does religion have to retreat before the progressive trend of science, but it is also exploited to become a tool for inhuman doctrines. He believes that it is necessary to restore the foundation of spiritual values ​​by studying the eternal truths in the universe, breaking down short-sighted dogmas that divide people, and complementing the imperfections of science to avoid humanity from entering the tragic state of destruction caused by wars, violence, and hatred that are breaking out everywhere in the present day.

Nguyen Phong

Chapter 1

If we observe events occurring in nature, we will see that life is inherently hidden, only its developments and effects are revealed. Science, thanks to observing this development, has come up with theories to explain phenomena in nature, such as plants growing from seeds, some creatures laying eggs, some species developing from fetuses... Today's science still cannot explain the sacred, invisible force that is silently promoting all life activities on this earth because it is hidden and cannot be observed with the naked eye or scientific instruments. Therefore, the science is still lacking and needs to be supplemented.

If we contemplate carefully, we will see that all phenomena in heaven and earth do not happen by chance or by chance but follow certain rules: Everything changes over time but cannot last forever and everything changes in cycles: born, mature, barren and then degenerate (

Birth, Persistence, Destruction, Destruction

) similar to the four seasons of weather: Spring, Summer, Fall, and Winter.

Since ancient times, Taoists and sages have experienced these natural laws and called them truth because they are immutable and do not change over time. Ancient sages believed that there was an invisible force in the universe, governing all things. Because of lack of an exact name, they temporarily called it "God's thought". They cite that thoughts come before actions, for example, before composing a painting, the artist must have an idea about that painting in his mind before painting it on the canvas. Before composing a piece of music, the musician must have the sound and rhythm in mind. Likewise, God thought of all things before they were formed and this stream of thought is the driving force behind all events in nature, motivating all activities of life. Sage Bruno1said to students:

“Weave a garment for God, through which you will see him, for through the visible things you will see the invisible.”

The religious leaders are those who have experienced and unified with this element, then drawn out rules appropriate to the level of human understanding at that time and taught them. We need to note that there are many truths proven by the teachers, but what they teach is very limited. The Buddha once told his disciples:

“What I know is as much as leaves in the forest, but what I teach you is just like a handful of leaves in my hand.”.

Jesus also told the apostles:

“I have many more things to say to you, but you cannot bear it now.” (S. John 16:12).

Another very important detail that few people pay attention to is that the religious leaders never founded a religion. They only teach what they have experienced to their students. It was their students who summarized those teachings into a system of thought with certain rules. Over time, this system of thought became a religion and the rules became dogma. If we go back to its origin, all religions stem from the inner experiences of the religious leaders through their understanding of the eternal truth in the universe. Therefore, no true religion can go against the truths of the universe.

Truth is the law of the universe so it never changes, but religion is a human explanation of truth so it is influenced by customs and traditions and is often changed to suit the circumstances of time and space. In the early stages of its establishment, religious laws were still in accordance with the teachings of the religious leaders, or in other words, in accordance with the truth of the universe. Religion has trained countless saints and sages whose talents and virtues have inspired and brought spiritual inspiration to millions of people afterward. Over time, some clergymen, due to lack of seriousness in practicing precepts and lack of spiritual experience, taught false truths or added more or less, causing religion, instead of being a living spiritual experience, to become a dry form of dogma and gradually degenerate. This has happened many times in the past, through ancient religions that few people know about today, and will happen in the future if we do not know how to preserve the noble spiritual inheritance that we are fortunate to inherit.

Let's review the history of Europe in the Middle Ages when religion held a unique position. Anything that went against the interpretation of the clergy at that time was considered heresy and the proponent was considered an apostate. This was the period when the quintessence of Christianity was greatly mis-teached, causing the charitable doctrine of the Savior to be modified into something“Theocracy”with blatant fabrications, aimed at serving the minority of kings in power.

The Middle Ages was a very dark era in European history, in the name of God, people created strict and unjust laws to oppress those who disagreed with them and caused bloody conflicts. The development of science in the Renaissance era overthrew these old narrow-minded concepts, laid the foundation for a democratic society, causing religion to gradually lose its influence on the masses and have to retreat before the progressive trend of science. Unfortunately, today's science is following the same old path, entering a unique position, and anything that goes against the explanations of scientists is considered“unscientific”and is not accepted. To overcome these extremes, people need to restore the spiritual and moral foundation through understanding the eternal truths in the universe, to break the short-sighted dogmas that divide people and complement the imperfections of science. Only true understanding and broad love can prevent humanity from the tragedies of destruction, suspicion, division, and violent hatred that are exploding all over the world.

Scientists need to know that the current scientific foundation built on the observation of external phenomena is lacking and needs to be supplemented with internal factors to be complete. Let's take the example of a scientist using a microscope to observe a phenomenon. He noted the developments and then proposed a theory to explain the above event. Shortly after, with the invention of the electron microscope, which could increase the lens intensity thousands of times, the scientist observed the above phenomenon again and discovered many new events that he did not know before. Therefore, the theory he proposed before is no longer correct. His initial observations were actually not wrong, but they were flawed and the theory proposed earlier was not perfect because it was built on an imperfect basis. Therefore, one should not hastily conclude that science can explain everything.

The object of science is external events that need to be supplemented with internal events through the study of hidden factors. Scientists need to return within themselves to understand the driving force that motivates them to research, invent and be aware of the role of science for people and society. In other words, in addition to developing knowledge, scientists must also be aware of their responsibilities in the great human family. Developing knowledge to benefit people is something that should be done, but if that invention only causes suffering to others, it should be avoided. Science without conscience is a disaster, knowledge without ethics is a great threat. An understanding person cannot contribute to things that cause division, conflict, or destruction of people.

Likewise, religious believers need to realize that over many centuries, religion has more or less changed, different from its original essence. The noun "Religion" originates from Latin

“Lier” means link. Religion connects people with God and religious leaders are entrusted with the mission of teaching people about this close relationship between people and God. Jesus said:

“It was not I who sent Me, but My Father sent Me.”. He brought to the world a message from God to those who know how to listen and sowed seeds of love so that they would bear fruit. He came to humanity not to establish a visible organization but to disseminate truths in the universe so that people can understand the laws of heaven and live accordingly. The organization was only set up after His death to learn about His instructions. It was very noble in the beginning but then it gradually changed and degenerated. This is not surprising because in the universe nothing can last forever, only the truth or the hidden aspect behind religion will last forever. The original teachings were often added, subtracted, and modified by later generations through discussions and debates about what He taught as well as the meaning of these teachings. As a result, religion is divided into different sects, each group explaining the truth according to their own understanding. This is the general situation of major religions today.

As a bishop, I feel it is time to speak out about the mistakes made in the Middle Ages when some clerics“simplify”religious elites to expand their influence. These people advocate that "nothing is worth spreading except what anyone can understand". The reduction of religious elites to a form of blind faith to serve the power of the minority created the seeds for today's religious divide. It is a fatal mistake when someone dares to assert that the highest teachings of the Savior are no different from the thoughts of a wise person or the morality of a lowly person that anyone can understand. It is unfortunate that over the years, many people have still accepted this concept without learning more about the deeper meanings and metaphors that the Savior taught to his students.

Some people think that everything necessary is already clearly written in the Bible and you just need to believe it, not understand it. They need to know that the Bible is written in a special language with profound metaphors and many meanings that a true believer needs to ponder carefully and cannot read in the form of a book."Where is the word, that is the meaning". Because of this blind trust, many scientists have taken advantage of the opportunity to prove that the stories in the Bible are absurd and unscientific, and then deny their value.

If one studies the history of all religions, one will see that the religious leaders often privately taught a few students things that the majority of the public could not comprehend. Almost every religion has two parts: exoteric and esoteric. The exoteric part is widely taught to everyone and is known in the form of rules and dogmas. The esoteric or religious essence is carefully preserved, only transmitted to selected people. Over time, the exoteric part can be modified to adapt to the circumstances of the time, but the esoteric part, which is the quintessence consistent with the spiritual experiences of the religious leaders, never changes.

Through historical documents, people see that in ancient times, Egyptian priests preserved their esoteric secrets in secret language (Hieroglyphic) that only a few disciples could learn. Likewise, the Greek sages selected a few students to transmit privately. The sage Pythagoras declared:

“One cannot feed sheep with research materials on herbs instead of grass, so only those who can digest spiritual food are worthy of entering my school.”. the Buddha Shakyamuni Buddha also said:

“I have the Dharma eye treasury, the wonderful mind of Nirvana, Not established in writing, The external teachings are transmitted exclusively to Mahakasyapa.”. The Bible also notes:

“When Jesus was alone, the twelve disciples came to Him and asked Him about these examples, and He answered:

'Examples are given to you to understand the mystery of the Kingdom of Heaven, but only for those who know how to put their understanding beyond figurative words, but for the majority of outsiders, all these things are just examples'

”. (Mark 4:10). One can understand that after the crowd had dispersed, some of his close disciples came to learn more with Him and He explained everything clearly to them.

Many people do not accept who Jesus taught in private and maintain that everything that needed to be said was already said to the masses by Him. They cite documents from medieval monks who recorded:

“You only need to believe, not understand because there is nothing to learn except what has been said that everyone knows.”. This is a narrow interpretation, devaluing the sublime truth taught by the Savior; Not only that, it also implies arrogance and contempt for people's understanding.

I feel it is my duty to refute such extravagant explanations and remind true believers to meditate on this verse.

“Do not leave holy things to dogs and do not throw pearls to swine.”(Mark 7:6). Obviously Jesus taught a lot, but not everyone can understand what He experienced. To the masses, He only taught what was appropriate to their abilities and level of understanding, but this did not mean that His teachings were as simple as that. Sometimes a simple sentence contains noble implications and profound assertions that others cannot understand. Only the close disciples who often gathered around Him were given instructions. Our duty today is to carefully meditate on His teachings and practice those loving teachings to restore the essences that He has instructed us.

As I stated above, the purpose of all religions is to improve and guide people to live in accordance with the eternal truths in the universe; promote the progress of humanity from barbarism and ignorance to perfection or Truth, Goodness, and Beauty; encourages the union of the human spirit with the divine element that pervades the universe to give

“God is all in all”(1 Cor. 15:28). In my opinion, the understanding of truth is the ladder that leads humanity to the common goal of perfection or goodness, but because everyone has different concepts or understanding, offering a common doctrine for all will not be of much benefit. What a wise person thinks is good, a fool cannot understand; What is suitable for the uneducated will give no pleasure to the learned scholar. Therefore, since ancient times, depending on customs and social conditions, religious leaders have appeared in many different places, teaching the truth in a form appropriate to the time and space at that time. Religion can be compared to the branches of a large tree whose root is the truth, because all religions originate from the inner experiences of the religious leaders through the understanding of the eternal truth in the universe. Therefore, no true religion can propose anything different from the immutable truth of the universe.

The important thing that people need to ask is whether religion currently improves life and brings true happiness to people? Is religion today still in line with the elites of the past? Does religion currently follow the original intentions of its founding leaders? These are not questions for debate because it only causes division and solves nothing, but are personal questions for people to ask themselves. As for me, even though I am a carefully trained bishop, I have had many times of wondering and questioning myself. After many years of thinking, I decided to find a teacher to learn more. Work

"religious teacher"This brought me to many places, studying with many famous teachers and finally coming into contact with sages in seclusion in the Snow Mountains.

As far as I know, these are people with a very high level of knowledge, and are responsible for preserving the spiritual fire of humanity, not allowing it to wither away over time. They rarely appear before the public but only work silently by sending out streams of noble and good thoughts to encourage those who are pursuing the spiritual path. Since ancient times, noble beings have appeared to guide humanity, from the time when humans were still eating feathers, living in caves, wearing animal skins until today's civilization. Nowadays, the sages who guide humanity all come from the ranks of people like us. They overcame many challenges and overcame difficulties to become sages. They are continuing the work of the noble teachers who have gone before them, teaching humanity to live in accordance with the truths of the universe, to become perfect and good according to the trend of evolution. What we need is to change our previous narrow, divisive concepts to develop a broader love. Instead of focusing on the differences between religions, people need to learn about the similarities of all religions to see that they all have a common purpose. Instead of looking for something new, people need to return to study the basic teachings that religious leaders have proposed and practice those teachings to build happiness for humanity.

The sections presented in this book are what I was taught. Of course, they are only outlines and not complete because my understanding is limited. I can say with certainty that what you know is a lot, but what you have taught me is only a very small part. Actually, these are not new things because they have been taught since ancient times in ashrams in China, Persia, India, Egypt, and Greece to a few carefully selected people.

Some things seem mysterious and hard to believe, but I don't ask readers to believe, I just hope you look back at your life and the events that have happened to draw lessons and compare them with what I present. Only when you clearly understand these things and see that they do not contradict your existing beliefs, can you apply them as a guideline for today's life.

If you have any spiritual inspiration or progress, I hope you will guide others so that together we can contribute to building a better world.

Chapter 2

Since ancient times, there have been religious leaders who appeared at important times to guide humanity. History has recorded ancient religions with religious leaders that few people know today, because their teachings only remain in vague legends. Nowadays, people often talk about the Hindu Lord Krishna, the Buddhist Shakyamuni Buddha, the Christian Jesus, because they are closer to us and their teachings are still widely circulated in today's society. However, in addition to those noble beings, there are countless other saints and sages, either directly studying with those religious leaders, or indirectly through the books they left behind, and are following their example to guide humanity. Some of these people work secretly, only recruiting a few students to teach religion, but do not show up or declare to people who they are. They are the ones who preserve humanity's spiritual treasure and their presence in the world is definitive proof of the value of truths in the universe that we unintentionally ignore.

In today's life, there are few people with faith and many people who doubt. Mentioning the presence of these anonymous sages only causes heated debate and is of no use, so even if they know, few people want to speak out. However, the time has come for me to speak up about these people and their teachings with the aim of restoring spiritual and moral values in today's society that focuses too much on material things and disregards spiritual traditions. In the name of science, some people have proposed unrealistic theories, causing suffering to people. To promote radical progress, those people rejected noble spiritual traditions and replaced them with atheistic doctrines.

During my trip to Tuyet Son, I met a number of sages who had a deeper level of understanding than we do. With respect, I asked them how they had reached such a level, and they all replied that not long ago, they were at the same level of evolution as we are now, and with diligent practice, one day, we will reach the same level as them. This simple answer is powerful evidence of the results of  spiritual practice. Up to now, many people have mistakenly believed that the great beings must be superheroes originating from somewhere, different from us, but few believe that they are all people like us, and with diligent practice, one day we can reach the same level as them.

All the sages I met were nothing unusual. Besides their leisurely appearance and calm demeanor, they are not much different from ordinary people, but once they meet them, everyone knows that they are in the presence of extraordinary people because of the noble vibrations emanating from them. Most of these people are quiet, perhaps they only speak up when they have a certain purpose. Most, however, are well-intentioned and possess a rich sense of humor; It must be added that the humor here is not meant to entertain but is a heart full of sympathy, not to offend others, but only to alleviate their concerns and worries.

Because these sages lived in seclusion on Snow Mountain, many people assumed that they must be from India or Tibet; but this is not true because I have met many people who come from the West, have white skin, blue eyes and dark blonde hair. They come from all over the world and operate on a large scale, far beyond the understanding of ordinary people, so we cannot conclude that they originate from a particular race or country. Someone asked me why do you live on Tuyet Son and not somewhere else? Many people have practiced in the deserts of the Middle East, some lived in the jungles of South America, but perhaps because Tuyet Son has mystical potential and occupies a special position in human history, many people have come here to retreat. This does not mean that other places do not have noble figures, but perhaps because of the Asian tradition of searching for monks and reverence for sages, they came to retreat here more than elsewhere.

When I came to study with these sages, I realized that they all possessed special abilities, far beyond the understanding of ordinary people. They consider everything with a different concept from us, because their minds no longer have any traces of greed and selfishness, commonly found in most people. To reach this level, they had to practice diligently to eliminate the lowly ego, to have a noble life, not for themselves, but for everyone. They have reached the level of complete control over body, speech, and mind, so there are no errors in actions, words, or thoughts. One of their most obvious characteristics is their complete development in all aspects. Most of us are imperfect, and few of us reach the highest level in every field. Even the wisest scientists only reach a certain level. Although far beyond their contemporaries, it cannot be called perfect in all aspects. We all have the seeds of certain characteristics; But for each person, depending on their personal evolutionary level, these characteristics develop or are hidden. On the contrary, sages are people who are completely developed in all aspects, and more specifically, their wisdom is far beyond ordinary people. They do not use ordinary reason with arguments like us, but use a transcendent intelligence that can understand everything in a general, clear and lucid way.

Most of the people I met had a very beautiful appearance. Maybe it's because they know how to live according to proper nutrition, without worries or worries, but it's also possible because their hearts are rich, so this inner strength has manifested, making their external appearance better. Later, I also learned that their bad karma had ended long ago, so their bodies had fully expressed the endless source of spiritual life.

Among the sages I have met, the most notable are three teachers to whom I owe great gratitude. These are sage Morya, sage Kuthumi and sage Djwal Kul. All three of them lived in a small valley hidden under vast snow-covered mountain peaks. Sages Morya and Kuthumi lived in two houses on opposite sides of the mountain, surrounded by a whispering green pine forest and at the bottom of the valley there was a stream with clear water flowing horizontally. Nearby is a stone bridge across the stream and a small temple where villagers sometimes come to burn incense and pray. Along the stream bank is a long winding trail, sometimes hidden and sometimes hidden around pomegranate bushes blooming with unusually beautiful colors. Because the valley is surrounded by very high mountains, very few people know, only the Tibetans living in nearby villages often come back and forth to worship Buddha at the temple at the bottom of the valley or a few lamas specializing in pharmacology and herbalism, who know the uses of exotic flowers in the area, so they come to pick medicine.

Sage Kuthumi's house is divided into two parts, with a hallway in the middle. Stepping through the main door is a quite large room, in the middle is a thick carpet that he often uses for meditation. Because the room has windows on three sides, sitting in the room, one can clearly observe the surrounding scenery. At the end of the room is a very old piano. Behind are bookshelves close to the wall. What surprised me was that in addition to very ancient books written by hand, there were also some modern European books. Sage Kuthumi is an erudite linguist who not only speaks and writes fluently in languages ​​such as English, French, and German but can also speak many local languages. In the house, there was also an old woman whom he called his sister and an old servant and his wife who took care of cooking, gardening and cleaning, but they rarely participated in teaching sessions for his disciples.

Sage Kuthumi incarnates as a North Indian from the Kashmir region, so his skin is as white as a European, his hair is long flowing down his shoulders, his eyes are clear and full of peace, his beard and hair are brown and shine golden in the sunlight. He has an extraordinary personality, difficult to describe because his whole body exudes an electric current full of charity that makes anyone who comes close to him feel unspeakably peaceful. He often sat quietly, immersed in a state of meditation. If one did not know, one might think that he was admiring the scenery, listening to the birds sing, or listening to the gurgling sound of stream water flowing down the stream; But in fact, he is working silently by sending out streams of noble electricity to all creatures around. Eastern people understand and respect meditation, so whenever they see him sitting still like that, no one dares to disturb him. It is obviously not easy for Westerners to accept the fact that a teacher just sits quietly and doesn't say anything all day like that. For them, a good teacher must be someone who speaks fluently and eloquently, teaching lofty theories to students with sublime, magical nouns. They cannot understand that Eastern teachers rarely teach with words but often with themselves, their lifestyle and behavior. Is it for this reason that sages often prefer to live in the East rather than the West?

Every day, his disciples, either from the surrounding villages or from far away regions, came to sit on the front porch to listen to his teachings. Sometimes he stepped out to teach them a few things, but other times he continued to meditate but no one bothered him. They are ready to receive a smile, a look of encouragement from him and respectfully sit still to receive the aura of peace emanating from the teacher they deeply respect. Sometimes he ate with them, but often he ate alone in his room. I don't know if he follows the Buddhist rule of only eating before noon or not, because during the time I lived here, I never saw him eat dinner. In my opinion, you don't need to eat every day and if you want, you can just tell your family to make a few simple dishes. Sometimes I saw him fasting for a whole month, but there were also times I saw him eating every day. His meals were very frugal, just a few small cakes, a bowl of porridge or a plate of fruit. He ate very slowly and leisurely and always practiced certain rituals, before and after eating.

When he needed to go somewhere, sage Kuthumi often rode a red-haired horse. It seems that horseback riding is his main exercise. He often went to nearby villages, visited several temples and talked with monks in the area. Sometimes the sage Morya accompanied him. This person often rides a beautiful white-haired horse. Although the two of them are the noblest teachers I have ever met, perhaps the surrounding villagers do not know much about them and only see them as very tolerant and gentle Tibetan noblemen.

Sage Morya lives in a house built of brick, with unique architecture and a large veranda in front of the door. He has a proud appearance, a well-proportioned body, and very bright, majestic eyes, expressing an authority that everyone who sees him must respect. His dark black hair falls down to his shoulders with a long beard, split into two parts. He was born as a minor king of Rajputana in India, so he had the majesty of a general. He often speaks short but powerful sentences that make people around him respectful.

Sage Djwal Kul lived in a simple house, built against the trunk of a very large ancient tree. He has a small body compared to sage Kuthumi or Morya, I don't know if he is Tibetan or Indian. He often travels here and there, spreading the Dharma and helping people everywhere, so he is rarely present in this valley.

These sages have achieved very high status so they can prolong their lives in this world to directly guide sentient beings. To adapt to this purpose of service, they, who are highly evolved souls, have chosen healthy bodies, families with special bloodlines, and taken very careful care of their bodies since it was still a life in the mother's womb. It is also necessary to add that the formation of a body is a very complex process, going through many special stages and when the soul reincarnates into a body, this body will be influenced by that person's karma. Depending on karma, the physical body gradually changes to become appropriate and reflect the inside, so a person who knows how to read appearance can partly predict a person's fate such as good, bad, bad, short or long life.

Obviously, human destiny is never completely certain but changes depending on surrounding factors, so Asians, especially Tibetans, know a very special fate conversion technique. According to the customs of this country, during the first seven years after birth, the soul greatly influences the body and continues to mold and change its shape to suit its karma. This is also the time when the child is greatly influenced by the parents and the surrounding environment, so parents can help the child through good deeds at this time. Although no one knows exactly what the individual's fate will be, according to tradition, within the first seven years, Tibetan families often try to give alms, release animals, and pray to dedicate merit to the child, create good conditions, and help the child's spiritual development. Perhaps so, most Tibetan families are spiritually inclined and one-fifth of the country's population has become monks.

According to Eastern tradition, a child is born into a family due to previous relationships, not by chance, so nurturing, caring for and educating the child is a very noble duty of parents. In contrast, the Western tradition views raising children as a responsibility that they must do for a certain period of time. Therefore, most people focus on material conditions and neglect the spiritual aspect. They are willing to spend large amounts of money to buy clothes and toys for their children, but few people spend time finding out what their tendencies or abilities are. Most people believe that spirituality is the responsibility of clergy and education is the responsibility of professors. Parents are only responsible for material aspects such as upbringing and clothing.

This is a major shortcoming, a spiritual degeneration because it reduces the role of parent to a responsibility before the law. Because it does not pay attention to ethics, Western society increasingly produces aggressive, hot-tempered people who always demand everything. A society consisting of such selfish and greedy individuals will not be able to progress in the long term and if there is no immediate solution, it will sooner or later be eliminated according to the general law of Evolution. This has happened many times in the past, through ancient civilizations that have declined and that few people know about today.

For the sages, their bodies are just the expression of the hidden source of life within. Thanks to taking care of them, they can maintain a healthy body and live much longer than ordinary people. I have met many people who appear to be middle-aged but in reality have lived over a hundred years old and some have lived for over two hundred years. A body structured to reflect such noble parts is very sensitive and must be carefully cared for, avoiding heavy, evil vibrations. Perhaps that's why saints and sages often live secluded lives, rarely setting foot in prosperous, urban places. Obviously, this prolonging life has a noble purpose, not the greed for life and fear of death as is common in most people.

According to my understanding, there are many sages who have achieved very high enlightenment status, but the number of people who decide to prolong their lives and stay in the mortal world for a while is not much. They received the special mission of maintaining the spiritual treasures of humanity and transmitting their knowledge to a number of carefully selected disciples. Depending on their background and level, these disciples can comprehend more or less. That time a disciple said his life had completely changed since learning these noble things, sage Kuthumi said:

“I have only revealed to you a small part of this sacred spiritual treasure. Depending on your efforts and progress, I will teach you more. Those who are determined to get closer to the truth, a mysterious path will open up for them."

Someone asked me how to meet such noble teachers: There must be a predestined relationship between teacher and student and depends on each individual's wishes. Asians have a saying:

“Like teacher, like student. A true teacher has no dishonest disciples, and evil people do not seek out sages.”. To find a true teacher, first of all that person must have a true heart and a sincere desire to seek the Dharma. One can only reach the sages by becoming pure and altruistic like them. They must know how to purify their ego, forget themselves, and devote themselves completely to the common cause like the sages are doing, then they will meet them. This can be explained by principle

“Same voice corresponds, same energy meets the same demand”. People with similar aspirations and interests will find each other.

Likewise, those who greedily seek magical powers or mysterious things will certainly meet magicians and witches who specialize in cultivating spells, magical powers, manipulations, or human manipulation. Those who are lazy, dependent, and just want to get results without putting in much effort will certainly meet evil teachers and evil friends who specialize in deceit, making a lot of promises for profit but with no results.

In the world, there are many selfish, greedy and curious people, but there are not many people who sincerely want to serve humanity, so when a person sincerely makes noble vows, he will definitely attract the true masters and sages immediately. These people will find ways to guide and create opportunities for them to come to them. The sages do not hesitate to help someone if they see that they have useful prospects in the future. They do not favor anyone but only think of the common good and evaluate the value of each person for the useful work they want to do.

Serving humanity is a big thing, requiring self-forgetfulness and serious character training, so anyone making vows will encounter unexpected challenges to test their sincerity and determination. Cause and effect (Karma) is a law that has been taught in most teachings of major religions. The cause is the seed, the cause; The fruit is the fruit, the result. The law of cause and effect teaches that causes always produce effects and that any cause will create that effect. Many people think that cause and effect is a theory of Buddhism, but in fact this is the truth of the universe that every religion talks about. the Buddha said:

“You reap what you sow”. The Hindu Lord Krishna also said:

i”. The Savior also said:

“Every driving force creates a similar and opposite reaction, the driving force and the reaction force are never separated.”. The word Karma in Indian means action but also has a reactionary meaning because action and reaction are never separated. Every time there is action, there is reaction, so everything is very closely related to each other.

Cause and effect is the law of the universe, so it is immutable, unlike human law, which often changes over time and space. The law of cause and effect is absolutely fair, it does not distinguish between rich and poor, noble or poor, king or commoner, while with human law, good people can be unjustly punished, evil people can escape the law. The rules of the law of cause and effect are so strict that nothing happens that is not influenced by it because any word, action or thought created has a reaction.

The Dhammapada mentions a disciple of the Buddha named Cakkhupala, who practiced diligently and had very high virtue but was blind. Other disciples then asked the Buddha why such a gentle, diligent practitioner suffered from blindness. The Buddha explained that in a previous life, this man was a talented physician who healed many people. A patient came to seek treatment and promised that if his illness was cured, he would work at the doctor's house for a while, but when his illness was cured, he broke his promise. The doctor was so angry that he changed the medicine, causing the patient to go blind. Because he blinded others, Cakkhupala had to pay the consequences in this life. He was born blind.

Many people do not accept the law of cause and effect because they see that some gentle people still suffer while evil people enjoy happiness. Those people have not mastered the current rules of the law of cause and effect because the process from action to reaction or from cause to effect does not have to happen immediately. A cause sown in the past can bear fruit in the present or the future, depending on the mysterious arrangement of other factors:

1/ Report: Whatever you do, you will have to suffer the consequences in the present life.

2/ Birth Report: Although the cause is caused, the effect is not yet ripe and will happen in the next life.

3/ After Report: The effect occurs because of a pre-existing cause.

Therefore, evil people sometimes enjoy good things at this time because of good reasons created before (After Report), not because of current evil deeds. In the same way, good people suffer misfortunes because of bad causes from the past, not because they do good things in the present. Because they lack the ability to see things clearly and comprehensively, many people make hasty judgments and conclude that there is no order or justice, but only competition, with the strong winning and the weak losing. Because they do not know about the law of cause and effect, many people live haphazardly, greedily and selfishly, causing suffering to others and will certainly reap the consequences of what they have done.

Where there is a cause, there must be an effect, so the amount of reward they have to pay will continue to increase over time. Because no one can pay off all these results in one life, that mass of causes becomes the driving force that leads people from one life to another, which is samsara (Reincarnation). People can decide their fate through personal efforts, they can advance or retreat, change or not change, but the wheel of evolution still rotates regularly and those who go against the laws of the universe will have to learn the necessary lessons. For example, a ferocious person who specializes in robbing and killing people without hesitation will enter the world beyond death to review his actions. From then on, he started thinking about his work. Obviously, not many people learn this lesson easily, but through many lives, when killing people, when being killed by others, there is constant resentment until one learns the real lesson: If you borrow, you will repay. If you do evil, you will receive evil. If you kill, you will be killed. Killing is wrong. At that time, in the face of slaughter, he will hesitate and not dare to do anything anymore. What people call conscience is the awareness of pre-existing experiences. A person who knows how to live with conscience means that he or she has learned the lesson that needs to be learned.

The sages of the Snow Mountain taught that each life gives people certain experiences that increase their understanding. After death, people enter a state of rest to draw on recent experiences. They will clearly see the mistakes they have made, the good things they have done, and reflect on the lessons they need to learn. Then, through the miraculous arrangement of the law of cause and effect, samsara, they are reincarnated into another situation to learn and experience more. These universal laws help humans summarize experiences into unique personalities or levels of personal evolution because each life is a necessary lesson. A person's personality is nothing more than his or her thoughts built on previous learning experiences. Therefore, people are the masters of their own destiny and whether they progress quickly or slowly is entirely up to them to decide. There are people who are lazy or arrogant and refuse to change, but the longer they continue on the path of life and death, the more bitterness they endure to learn. Meanwhile, a knowledgeable person, thanks to knowing how to change to live according to the laws of the universe, can easily step into the clouds, leisurely and freely enter realms of bliss and nobility.

Some people do not accept that humans have their own will, but believe that everything depends on God's will and explain God's will as a "God" who has the power to determine fate and that people cannot change. However, this concept has been outdated for a long time. Through the teachings of the Savior, we see a "God" who, depending on inspiration, gives good conditions to some people and torments others to bad situations, which is unacceptable. Jesus taught:

“God is a loving father who loves us very much”. If we believe in Him, how can we accept the notion that humans are just weak victims, without will, completely dependent on the punishment of such a "fiend"!

How people are born or under what circumstances is entirely due to previous causes, determined by the laws of cause and effect, and not by the decision of any power. A noble person is a soul that has progressed, learned and changed, over thousands of lives. An evil person is a soul that is still immature and has not yet learned much, so it still has to go through a lot of bitterness and suffering to learn the necessary lesson. The difference between people is nothing more than maturity in the level of evolution and understanding. Ask yourself, if life is only short in one lifetime, what is the point of sacrificing and helping others? What benefit would a hero sacrifice his life for his country, if not that country would lose a talented person? The same goes for saints who martyred themselves for their faith. If death is the end, wouldn't humanity be at a disadvantage because of losing noble people? According to the law of cause and effect and samsara, the sacrifices of those people are not meaningless, because it will become a lesson for others, helping others to follow their example of sacrifice. As for them personally, knowing how to forget themselves to serve an ideal will help them become more perfect because in the future they will return to guide humanity.

Some time ago, a psychologist created a theory about the influence of the surrounding environment on human temperament. Psychologists have invented educational methods to shape children into certain patterns. However, anyone who has ever been a parent has seen that each child has a special personality and talent, and no two children are the same. Education can only partially shape and modify, but cannot overcome the existing natural nature. If we observe, we will see that there are children who are aggressive from an early age that schools cannot teach, and there are children who, despite living in the worst circumstances, still become saints. Only an understanding of the laws of the universe can explain that depending on personal evolution, through thousands of samsara lives, people's personalities are different. Any pressure to mold people in a particular direction cannot bring positive results.

In other words, whether a country progresses or declines depends on whether its people have a high or low level of knowledge and evolution. Souls that are less evolved, more aggressive, and more barbaric are often reincarnated in places where the intellectual level is low and society is less developed. On the contrary, a nation becomes prosperous thanks to souls with profound understanding coming to reincarnate to help and bring good things.

Debts, resentments and relationships will be arranged and arranged in the world beyond death, not in the present life.

Many people do not believe in samsara but think that after death the human soul will immediately go to heaven or hell. This is an incorrect concept because it implies a complete change after death: Or that person gives up all bad habits, becomes a saint and goes to heaven; Or that person must abandon all good qualities, put on all sins, become a devilish demon and be damned to hell. A benevolent and compassionate God cannot play "luck" like that, because any change must happen gradually and cannot be so sudden. The truth is, whatever a person is like when they are alive, their nature will be the same when they die, it doesn't change at all. If when they are alive they love to eat and drink, then after death they will still love to drink and eat. If they love God and people while they are alive, they will still have the same heart after death. Death is just the removal of the physical garment, but the soul changes nothing! The earthly world or the world beyond death's door are also worlds in the universe and must be governed by the laws of the universe and cannot be otherwise.

Understanding the law of samsara is very useful, it helps people have a calm attitude in the face of adversity because they know that everything has a pre-existing cause, not luck. People who understand cause and effect and samsara will not be jealous of those with a higher status than themselves, will not despise those who are inferior to them, but will have a broad, generous, and tolerant view of life in the face of changes in times.

Why is it that among the billions of people living on earth, no one is the same? In human history, there have been individuals who developed perfectly in all aspects and became transcendent people that we call teachers, saints, and sages. The presence of these people is proof that there is a clear path of spiritual evolution that, if followed, we will also reach that level of splendor and goodness. This is the basis of the Law of Evolution because everything, invisible or visible, low or high, noble or inferior, is developing towards a noble goal. Evolution is the manifestation of the hidden life force in all things in space and time. Although the form changes, the spirit inside remains constant because it is the divine life, originating from the noble, boundless source of life expressed through countless forms in the universe. In the process of learning, people will change their minds, from crude to noble, just like students must start from elementary school and high school before entering university. Many people do not believe that inanimate species such as rocks and plants can evolve, but the laws of the universe make no distinction. Thanks to more evolution, plants can receive very limited vibrations. The development of animals goes hand in hand with the development of the emotional bodies and especially the development of the soul. A virtuous action, no matter how small, can be the drop of water that sprouts a seed; A sincere word can alert those around you and make them know how to return to the right path. Sage Kuthumi said:

“When a person knows how to devote themselves to serving, for the common good of humanity, they don't have to worry about anything anymore. Once they have contributed to serving the heavenly plan of the noble beings, they will take good care of them."

Because the future world will be completely different from today's world and humanity in the future will have a level of understanding far different from humanity today, there have long been activities to quietly sow the seeds of noble ideas to prepare and promote humanity's evolution. Along with that, there are destructive effects that change and overturn all existing values because it is only in decline and suffering that people become aware of noble values. Therefore, before this golden age occurs, humanity must go through a period of darkness and decadence to destroy fake material values before a noble spiritual value is promoted. This is the time when humanity will realize that all the suffering in the world today originates from selfishness and greed due to lack of love. If everyone knows how to love and treat each other as brothers, regardless of nationality, race, or religion, all conflicts and disputes will disappear and a glorious age will come to humanity. Therefore, knowledgeable people need to make efforts to repair their character to prepare for the coming period. Many people think that this requires a high level of knowledge or some iron discipline, but in fact this is not true because the truth is not something beyond human understanding, on the contrary, it is very simple and can be applied to everyone. Here are a few basic rules:

1/ To prepare for cultivating one's mind and character, people need to have basic knowledge of universal laws such as samsara, cause and effect, evolution... These laws are still presented in one form or another through religions, or depending on personal learning experience and understanding. For example, a person who does not believe in cause and effect and thinks that they can do whatever they want without paying any price will certainly encounter very unexpected consequences for their actions. Likewise, a person who lives a greedy, selfish life will find that satisfying material needs cannot bring true happiness, because it can never satisfy the desire of the inner spirit. The more materially satisfied they become, the more their greed urges them to seek more, to get one thing and then ask for another and so on until death. Greed does not stop here but continues to dominate and motivate them to rush headlong into material ambitions for countless samsara lives. Only when they know that material desires never end because it is really not the purpose of life, but only the satisfaction of spiritual needs can bring true peace. Only then will they realize that real people are spiritual, not material.

If for whatever reason people still cannot understand the above-mentioned universal laws clearly, they should at least believe that these are the basic things that should be followed to have a peaceful and comfortable life. The Law of Evolution states that humans can only achieve perfection by living a good life, obeying the eternal laws of the universe. They will go through countless lives to learn the necessary lessons, to progress and develop until they reach the level of perfection. The more they learn, the more clearly they see the justice of the laws of the universe. Once they know how to obey and live according to these laws, they will find the true noble purpose of life.

2/ In addition to understanding the laws of the universe, people need to know how to direct their thoughts to noble and good things, not to be attracted by thoughts of greed and selfishness. In today's social life, almost everyone is influenced by a chaotic lifestyle, so keeping a calm and undisturbed soul is very difficult. One of the methods of calming the mind is the practice of meditation that I mentioned above, but not everyone can practice this method. Therefore, I often encourage some people to focus their thoughts on the images of their teachers such as Jesus or the Buddha, and then ask themselves:

What must I do to live a life like yours? How should I change so that I can demonstrate their goodness to those around me?

These thoughts will help their souls stay focused on a clear purpose, not being drawn in by evil meanings. Once the thoughts are pure, without malice, people will not be able to act differently. A pure thought is also about seeing only the truth. To do so, people need to put aside public opinions and prejudices to look straight at the truth as it is.

Most people are easy-going and do not pay attention, so they are easily attracted to prejudices. Once they think someone is bad, all of that person's actions and words are bad. Obviously people are inherently imperfect and have both good and bad qualities, but why do we only pay attention to that person's bad qualities and forget that they also have good qualities? We only see a certain aspect and then immediately jump to conclusions, so our thoughts are not genuine, not benevolent, and not correct. Jesus taught:

“All people are children of God”, if you truly believe in Him, why can brothers of the same father hate each other? Jesus' teachings are great sermons on love, but why don't those who want to follow His example have loving and tolerant thoughts like Him?

3/ In addition to directing thoughts to noble things, people need to be conscious of mastering their speech because language is the main means of communication between people. You should only say good things that are true and not say bad things about others. Many stories told about someone are often not true and if people continue to repeat this, then what that person says will not be true. Thus they harm themselves, because they have created a bad cause and any cause will bring the same result. Even if that is true, the person who repeats it is still wrong, because they do not help anyone by repeating the wrongs of others. Therefore, people need to practice keeping silent and not mentioning anything about those useless things. Many people believe that polite people must know how to speak because being silent is rude and unsocial, so whenever they meet someone they chatter endlessly. Actually, polite people are people who know how to listen, not people who know how to talk. Jesus warned:

“For every superfluous, useless word you utter, you will have to answer on the Last Judgment Day.”. If we believe in Him, why can we continue to talk so carelessly?

4/ In addition to keeping thoughts and words carefully, people need to act uprightly, truthfully, and with conscience. All three things: Thinking, speaking and acting are very closely related to each other, because if we keep our thoughts pure and our words straight, how can people do things that go against their conscience? Before acting, people need to consider whether doing so will cause harm to anyone. In today's hurried society, many people often act haphazardly and unconsciously, not knowing that every action has results and a careless action will bring negative consequences for themselves and for others. Not doing evil is not enough, we must also actively do good. the Buddha taught:

“Avoid doing evil, only do good”. If we believe in Him, why could we do otherwise?

In my opinion, an upright action is a correct action, not self-interested, not selfish, and thus is already an action that serves the world. Many people think that serving must be great and great things, but few people know that thinking, speaking and acting according to the truth are the stepping stones to building a loving and good society for the future. Some other people think that the things I have presented above are too simple, trivial, and cannot be changed. They advocate that in order to change, there must be great, great, sublime projects, but does humanity already have too many great projects like that? If we observe, we will see that sometimes great deeds are selfish deeds because the initiator often wishes to achieve something, if not profit, then fame. Serving humanity is not about big, great things, but about selfless things. Don't think about what we like to do or want to do, but think about what we need to do, no matter how small and trivial it is. We need to know that each individual's words, thoughts and actions affect others more or less. Try to imagine a society in which everyone only works without calculating personal gain, speaks gently and politely in the spirit of mutual love, how good would that society be?

We need to know that action is not a human ability but a power entrusted to humans by God for them to use and they must be responsible for their actions. These powers are useful tools for people to share and help each other to build a world in which love is the main basis. This universe was created by love and exists only in love. Any action must reflect this love because if used for other purposes, it is an abuse of power and people will have to pay a very high price for their error.

5/ In addition to cultivating the mind and character, people need to know how to choose true karma professions, means of livelihood that do not harm people or animals, or cause damage to any living creature. Obviously, professions such as butchering and selling alcohol are not professions that bring good results, because they harm the lives of other creatures. Many people think that they have to work to make a living, but they have the right to choose a karma profession and that things that cause suffering to other living beings will create suffering consequences for themselves.

In addition, even doing righteous karma professions but with a dishonest mind also becomes unjust because of its consequences. A professor who is not dedicated to teaching but only cares about scolding and treating students unfairly will train generations of aggressive and violent students. A doctor who is not dedicated to patient care but only cares about profiteering will reap adverse consequences later. The salesperson knows the quality of the goods better than anyone else, but if the goods are bad and are said to be good, then they have gone against the grain and the business is no longer a genuine profession but becomes a fraud. When others believe in you, it is an honor that you must repay appropriately because a knowledgeable person must be aware that karma is not just a job to make a living but also a vocation, a duty to society.

6/ In addition to cultivating the mind and character and doing genuine karma jobs, people also have a duty to preserve their health and abilities. Most people are born with physical and mental abilities and they need to know how to save and not waste these abilities because action is power and abuse of power will bring unfortunate consequences.

To live, people must eat and drink but should not abuse it to avoid diseases that are caused by this indiscriminate eating. Eating too much means taking away others' food. In nature, everything is perfectly balanced, including the amount of food needed to nourish all living things. The reason why there is famine is because rich and powerful countries consume food wastefully and indiscriminately, creating an imbalance. If we observe, we will see that every time there is a famine, in other countries, the number of people suffering from diseases as a result of indiscriminate eating also increases greatly. In civilized societies, many people eat carelessly and unconsciously. Not only do they consume a lot, but they also always demand delicious and strange things; Therefore, the number of people suffering from incurable diseases also increased seriously. People blame germs, hygiene and environmental issues, but no one takes responsibility for their own stomach needs. A knowledgeable person needs to be well aware of this nutritional issue and its consequences. Not only to avoid illness but also to extend compassion to those who are less fortunate and do not have enough food and clothing. Saving food and eating just enough is a discipline that helps people reduce material desires, reduce greed and selfish thoughts, and helps their own health.

7/ Finally, people need to take time for self-examination and introspection. We need to know clearly who we are, what our duties are, what role we play in the current situation, and what we must do to be worthy of our status as a human being in society. Life is a series of experiences, happy as well as sad, suffering as well as happy, but people must know how to choose things to learn, to meditate on, to gain experience. You must know how to live comfortably and innocently, know how to forgive, let go of the things others do that bother you and remember the good things they do for you to fill your soul with gratitude. Living in society is a debt to humanity, we need to be grateful to everyone. From food to clothes to countless other products, they are all products of society; and once our hearts are filled with this gratitude, we will look at society with a completely different perspective.

In short, to live in a good world with a high level of evolution in the upcoming cycle, people need to repair their bodies and minds right now. If everyone repairs and helps each other move forward, the path to that future world will not be far.

Conclusion

The ancients had a saying "The blue sea becomes a mulberry field" to refer to changes over time because change is inevitable in the evolutionary schedule of humanity. Once upon a time, the vast continent of Lemuria still lay across the earth along the equator, but now it has disintegrated into countless small islands in the Pacific Ocean! Once upon a time, the majestic continent of Atlantis with its brilliant golden pyramid-shaped architecture has now sunk deep into the ocean, leaving no trace! Everything changes, everything is impermanence, everything disintegrates over time, dust will return to dust because if there is prosperity, there must be decline, if there is success, there must be destruction and that is the eternal, unchanging law of the universe. However, the law of the universe also dictates that only with destruction can there be creation, with destruction can there be success, so there have been civilizations that decline and then develop at a different time according to the variation of the Law of Cycles, each cycle is a change and evolution to reach completeness and unity. Only if Lemuria breaks up will there be Asia and Australia; Only when the Atlantis civilization declined did the Egyptian and South American civilizations arise.

Today, civilized people often pride themselves on being able to dominate nature and control everything; But that is just a wild illusion of those who do not understand. If they understand that humans are just small creatures living on fragile solutions on the earth's surface and just one seismic change will change everything. The Law of Cycles shows that ancient races and civilizations have developed and declined according to seismic changes, so this will certainly happen in the future, it cannot be otherwise. Currently, civilized humans are destroying the earth, destroying the environment, and destroying other living things calmly and mercilessly, without realizing that they are promoting seismic changes so that it happens faster than ever.

Someone asked me if I wanted to present a new theory or a new form of belief when writing this book. I would like to affirm that all of what I have presented is absolutely nothing new, but on the contrary, it is as old as the earth. All of this was taught in ancient ashrams in China, Persia, Tibet, Egypt, and Greece to carefully selected people. People can find these rules in the scriptures of major religions if they take the time to return, read, understand and practice the noble teachings of the founding fathers. I do not intend to introduce anything new but simply present the basic universal laws such as samsara, cause and effect and Evolution, which have been taught for thousands of years. Many people probably just want to know about mysterious and strange things because they are curious and do not want to hear about anything normal or simple, but the laws of the universe are not chapters to criticize or discuss. God did not create the universe for fun or entertainment. He does not set up laws for humans to study, but for His children to live by them and find their way back to unity with Him.

Is humanity today progressing or corrupting? Some people think that humans have come very far through inventions, discoveries and material comforts, but there are also people who think that humans have degenerated a lot because today's life is no longer as comfortable and peaceful as before. Obviously, based on scientific standards, humans have advanced a lot compared to hundreds of years ago, but is science the solution for human life? Does science really bring happiness to people? Why is the more civilized society is, the more people suffer? The more a country progresses, the more dissatisfied and uncomfortable people feel? Because people believe too much in the glamor of science, they have forgotten that science has never solved basic human desires. Over the past centuries, many scientific theories have been proposed, replacing old, outdated theories. In the future, today's scientific theories will certainly change and things built on old foundations will be eliminated. Just like that, people continue to follow one theory after another and life is turned into a laboratory with never-ending experiments. Are the scientific theories that come from rational minds just layers of paint on the outside to cover up the damage that has rusted from the inside? People have done experiments by changing the regime, law, economy, society as well as religion, but what has this change brought other than feelings of confusion, fear, insecurity, hatred, violence and division? Is it true that real change has not happened because people do not know where to look and still dive headlong into the adventures and risks of exciting scientific theories?

To solve humanity's current problems, people need to know how to go back and turn back the pages of old books to review the teachings of the Patriarchs and clearly understand their teachings about the laws of the universe. Only when people clearly understand the relationship between humans, between humans and God, know clearly the realms of nature, and about life after death, will they realize that humans are truly the spiritual part that is always shining, the spark of God, an eternal life, not this tangible body that is now gone. Only when people understand clearly about the creation of the universe, about the laws of the universe such as the laws of Cycle, Evolution, samsara, cause and effect and know accordingly to repair, to change their lives in accordance with divine evolution, will they understand the purpose and meaning of life.

The future of humanity will completely depend on the level of sacrifice, sincerity, and especially the knowledge and wisdom that each person experiences because human spiritual maturity will occur naturally with understanding to turn this world full of strife and hatred into a world full of love. This universe was created by love, by love and only exists in sincere love.
